questions.text:
A variable x is said to be live at a statement [latex]S_{i}[/latex] in a program if the following three conditions hold simultaneously:
i. There exists a statement [latex]S_{j}[/latex] that uses x
ii. There is a path from [latex]S_{i}[/latex] to [latex]S_{j}[/latex] in the flow graph corresponding to the program
iii. The path has no intervening assignment to x including at [latex]S_{i}[/latex] and [latex]S_{j}[/latex]

The variables which are live both at the statement in basic block 2 and at the statement in basic block 3 of the above control flow graph are
questions.solution:
Live-in = use [latex]\cup[/latex] (live-out [latex]-[/latex] def).

- Block 1 uses q, r, v before defining them [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] in(1) = {q, r, v}
- in(4) = {v, r} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(1) [latex]-[/latex] {q}) = {r, v}
- in(2) = {r, u} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(4) [latex]-[/latex] {v}) = {r, u}
- in(3) = {s, u} [latex]\cup[/latex] (in(4) [latex]-[/latex] {q}) = {r, s, u, v}

Common: r, u

Answer: r, u

r, s, u

q,v

questions.text: Which one of the following is TRUE at any valid state in shift-reduce parsing?
questions.solution:
In a valid shift-reduce parse, the stack content is always a viable prefix, i.e. a prefix of some right sentential form that does not go past the handle.

Answer: The stack contains only a set of viable prefixes

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Viable prefixes appear only at the bottom of the stack and not inside
Viable prefixes appear only at the top of the stack and not inside
The stack contains only a set of viable prefixes
The stack never contains viable prefixes

questions.text:
Consider the following grammar.
[latex]\mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{AB}[/latex]
[latex]\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{a}[/latex]
[latex]\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaB}[/latex]
[latex]\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{bbA}[/latex]
Which of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- |A| = 1 or 2|B| + 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always odd; |B| = 2 + |A| [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] odd; |S| = odd + odd = even. So 1 and 3 are true.
- a's only come from A, separated by B's that contain b's [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no "aaa". True.
- But [latex]B\Rightarrow bbA\Rightarrow bbBaB\Rightarrow bb\,bbA\,aB[/latex] gives "bbbb". So statement 4 is FALSE.

Answer: No string produced by this grammar has four consecutive b's

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The length of every string produced by this grammar is even
No string produced by this grammar has three consecutive a's
The length of substring produced by B is always odd
No string produced by this grammar has four consecutive b's

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT represented in a subroutine's activation record frame for a stack-based programming language?
questions.solution:
An activation record holds local variables, return address, parameters, and links for non-local access. The heap is a separate memory area, not part of any stack frame.

Answer: Heap area

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Values of local variables
Return address
Heap area
Information needed to access non local variables
